purpose: Define outcome-oriented participation metrics for the redesigned BetterMakati participation system before any new instrumentation or public dashboard is added.
implementationBoundary: This file defines populations, events, numerators, denominators and interpretation rules only. W3R-10a does not add analytics, tracking events, contributor identifiers, API fields, aggregates or public metrics.
principles: Measure useful progression and evidence, not participation volume for its own sake.
A BetterMakati workflow event is not automatically evidence of City Government receipt, action or resolution.
Case-stage metrics use explicit lifecycle evidence rather than GitHub open/closed state alone.
Forwarded means BetterMakati documented a referral attempt; acknowledged requires a separate authority-acknowledged lifecycle event.
Action reported means action evidence was recorded; it is not automatically a resolution.
Community-verified resolved is the strongest BetterMakati case-resolution state and remains distinct from a community comment that merely says a problem appears resolved.
Observations are dated condition snapshots, not complaints, cases, ratings or canonical place facts.
Observation freshness is based on observedAt, not submittedAt.
Civic-audit coverage is calculated only against the campaign's frozen target set and cannot be extrapolated beyond that set.
Anonymous public aliases, IP addresses and free-text names must not be treated as stable contributor identities.
Any future repeat-contribution measurement must use a privacy-preserving contributor key and must not expose individual participation histories.
Every published rate must state its population, time window, sample size and evidence basis. Publication thresholds are defined separately in W3R-10b.

included: Civic reports and proposals stored as BetterMakati civic cases.
Documented civic-case lifecycle events: reviewed, forwarded, acknowledged, action-reported and community-verified-resolved.
Civic-audit campaigns with frozen target sets and entity-complete rules.
notCombinedIntoCaseLifecycle: General BetterMakati proposals, ideas, corrections, sources, volunteer offers and contact submissions from /api/feedback.
Official consultations or hearings hosted by government.
Fallback URLs that were generated but not confirmed as submitted.
Emergency attempts rejected before BetterMakati case creation.
scope.reasonForSeparation: These workflows do not currently share equivalent lifecycle evidence. Combining unlike records would produce misleading funnel rates.

canonicalDefinitions.eligibleCivicCase: A native BetterMakati civic report or proposal successfully created as a civic issue. Emergency attempts rejected before creation, fallback-only unsaved attempts, structured observations and general feedback are excluded.
canonicalDefinitions.caseCohort: Eligible civic cases whose issue-created timestamp falls inside the selected reporting period. Later lifecycle outcomes remain attached to the original submission cohort.
canonicalDefinitions.firstStageEvent: The earliest valid civic-admin event for the specified lifecycle status.
canonicalDefinitions.reviewed: At least one valid civic-admin event with status=reviewed.
canonicalDefinitions.routed: At least one valid civic-admin event with status=forwarded. A routed case documents BetterMakati's referral attempt; it does not prove authority receipt.
canonicalDefinitions.acknowledged: At least one valid civic-admin event with status=acknowledged. This is the first lifecycle state that may be described as documented authority acknowledgement when the event identifies the responsible authority/body.
canonicalDefinitions.actionReported: At least one valid civic-admin event with status=action-reported.
canonicalDefinitions.documentedResolution: At least one valid civic-admin event with status=community-verified-resolved.
canonicalDefinitions.communityResolutionSignal: An ordinary community comment with commentType=resolved. This is evidence to review, not the documentedResolution state.
canonicalDefinitions.substantiveObservation: A stored structured observation answer that is not a not-observed value.
canonicalDefinitions.campaignObservedEntity: A frozen campaign target with at least one valid campaign-period observation.
canonicalDefinitions.campaignCompleteEntity: A frozen campaign target satisfying the campaign's minimumObservationsPerEntity and required-question substantive-answer rule.

metricFamilies.label: Civic case progression
metricFamilies.cohortRule: Use submission cohorts based on civic case createdAt. Do not build the denominator from cases that merely happen to be open or updated during the reporting period.

metrics.label: Reviewed case share
metrics.question: Of civic cases submitted in the cohort, how many received documented BetterMakati review?
metrics.numerator: Eligible civic cases in the cohort with a reviewed lifecycle event.
metrics.denominator: All eligible civic cases in the cohort.
metrics.interpretation: Measures BetterMakati review coverage, not government response.

metrics.label: Routed case share
metrics.question: Of civic cases submitted in the cohort, how many have a documented BetterMakati referral?
metrics.numerator: Eligible civic cases in the cohort with a forwarded lifecycle event.
metrics.denominator: All eligible civic cases in the cohort.
metrics.interpretation: Measures documented BetterMakati routing/referral. It must not be labeled authority receipt or acceptance.

supportingDiagnostic.numerator: Routed cases whose first forwarded event includes both authority and channel.
supportingDiagnostic.purpose: Check whether a routing claim is supported by a named destination and delivery channel.

metrics.label: Authority acknowledgement share
metrics.question: Of civic cases submitted in the cohort, how many later obtained documented authority acknowledgement?
metrics.numerator: Eligible civic cases in the cohort with an acknowledged lifecycle event.
metrics.denominator: All eligible civic cases in the cohort.
metrics.evidenceRule: For public presentation as authority acknowledgement, the lifecycle event must identify the responsible authority/body. A forwarded event alone never satisfies this metric.
metrics.interpretation: Measures documented acknowledgement visible to BetterMakati, not all acknowledgements that may have occurred outside the recorded workflow.

metrics.label: Action-evidence share
metrics.question: Of civic cases submitted in the cohort, how many have later documented action evidence?
metrics.numerator: Eligible civic cases in the cohort with an action-reported lifecycle event.
metrics.denominator: All eligible civic cases in the cohort.
metrics.interpretation: Records that some action was evidenced; it does not imply the issue was fully resolved or that BetterMakati independently verified the quality of the action.

metrics.label: Documented resolution share
metrics.question: Of civic cases submitted in the cohort, how many reached BetterMakati's documented community-verified resolution state?
metrics.numerator: Eligible civic cases in the cohort with a community-verified-resolved lifecycle event.
metrics.denominator: All eligible civic cases in the cohort.
exclusions: GitHub issue closed without a community-verified-resolved lifecycle event.
Ordinary community resolved comments without the lifecycle event.
Action-reported events without later documented resolution.
metrics.interpretation: Measures cases with documented BetterMakati resolution evidence. It is not a claim that every unresolved cohort case remains unresolved in the real world.

metricFamilies.presentationRule: Lifecycle shares may be displayed as a progression only if the selected cohort and denominator remain the same across stages. Conditional stage-to-stage rates may be calculated internally later but must not replace the cohort-based shares without explicit labeling.

metricFamilies.label: Condition observation freshness

metrics.label: Latest observation age
metrics.entityLevelCalculation: asOf minus the entity's latest valid observedAt
metrics.population: Canonical civic entities with at least one valid structured observation.
metrics.interpretation: Lower age means more recently observed conditions. It is not a quality score.

metrics.label: Observed entity count
metrics.calculation: Count of canonical entities with at least one valid structured observation in the selected period or all-time view.
metrics.interpretation: Coverage count only; it must be shown with the eligible entity population when used as a coverage statement.

metricFamilies.thresholdBoundary: W3R-10a does not define a universal fresh/stale cutoff. Any age threshold for public labels belongs to W3R-10b and may vary by observation family.

metricFamilies.label: Civic audit coverage

metrics.label: Target entities observed
metrics.numerator: Frozen target entities with at least one valid observation whose observedAt falls inside the campaign period.
metrics.denominator: All frozen target entities in the campaign.

metrics.label: Target entities meeting the campaign completion rule
metrics.numerator: Frozen target entities satisfying minimumObservationsPerEntity and required-question substantive-answer coverage.
metrics.denominator: All frozen target entities in the campaign.

metricFamilies.interpretation: These are operational coverage measures. They do not score, rank or judge the condition of target places.
metricFamilies.scopeRule: Never replace the frozen target denominator with all parks, all barangays or all Makati places unless the campaign itself froze and justified that exact scope.

metricFamilies.label: Repeat contribution

metrics.label: Repeat contributor share
metrics.question: Among contributors measurable with a privacy-preserving stable key in the selected period, what share made more than one valid contribution?
metrics.numerator: Distinct privacy-preserving contributor keys associated with at least two valid contributions in the selected period.
metrics.denominator: Distinct privacy-preserving contributor keys associated with at least one valid contribution in the selected period.
metrics.deduplicationRule: A duplicate submission that resolves to an already-existing record does not create an additional contribution event unless the user adds a new substantive confirmation, support or observation.
metrics.interpretation: Measures repeat participation among contributors who can be measured consistently; it does not measure unique residents.

metrics.label: Repeat contribution events
metrics.calculation: Count valid contribution events after a contributor's first valid contribution in the selected period.
metrics.interpretation: A workload/engagement diagnostic. It should not be used to rank or publicly profile contributors.

privacyRequirements: Do not use IP address as the stable contributor key.
Do not treat publicAlias or free-text name as identity.
Do not require a public account solely to measure this metric.
A future contributor key should be pseudonymous, non-public and documented with retention rules before W3R-10c instrumentation.
metricFamilies.currentReadiness: Current data cannot produce a trustworthy repeat-contributor rate because anonymous submissions do not carry a stable privacy-safe identity key.

crossCuttingRules.timeWindows: Every aggregate requires an explicit asOf and reporting window. Case funnels use submission cohorts; observation and audit metrics use observedAt.
crossCuttingRules.lateOutcomes: A lifecycle event that occurs after the cohort period still counts toward that cohort when measuring mature outcomes as of a later date.
crossCuttingRules.rightCensoring: Recent cohorts have had less time to reach later stages. W3R-10b must define age/maturity thresholds before later-stage rates are publicly compared across periods.
crossCuttingRules.zeroDenominator: Return not-applicable rather than 0% when a denominator is zero.
crossCuttingRules.duplicateCases: Cases prevented by duplicate detection are not new case submissions. Community confirmations/support may be reported separately but must not inflate submitted-case denominators.
crossCuttingRules.fallbackOnly: Generating a fallback URL is not a successful BetterMakati submission and must not enter native case/submission outcome denominators unless completion can be independently confirmed.
crossCuttingRules.evidenceSeparation: Community comments, BetterMakati lifecycle events and government acknowledgement/action must remain distinguishable in both storage and presentation.
crossCuttingRules.barangayBreakdowns: A barangay breakdown is valid only when the underlying record has a canonical barangay/entity relationship or explicit barangay scope. Do not infer local attribution from free-text mentions alone.
crossCuttingRules.noPopularityLeaderboard: Do not turn counts, repeat contribution or audit participation into contributor, barangay or place popularity rankings.

currentDataReadiness.review: derivable from civic-admin reviewed events plus civic case createdAt
currentDataReadiness.routing: derivable from civic-admin forwarded events plus civic case createdAt
currentDataReadiness.acknowledgement: partially derivable; public authority-acknowledgement metric additionally requires a named authority/body on the event
currentDataReadiness.observationFreshness: derivable from structured observation observedAt values
currentDataReadiness.auditCoverage: derivable from frozen campaign targets plus campaign-period observations
currentDataReadiness.repeatContribution: not reliably derivable until a privacy-preserving stable contributor key exists

nextStep.title: Define metric publication thresholds
nextStep.scope: Separate internal operational metrics from public metrics and set minimum sample, cohort-maturity, freshness and coverage thresholds. No dashboards or instrumentation.
